subject: Chemistry
title: Preparing a Pure, Dry Soluble Salt

blocks.learningGoal: Select a suitable acid and insoluble solid, then explain the route to pure, dry salt crystals.

content.centralQuestion: How can we prepare pure, dry crystals of a soluble salt?
objectives: Choose reactants for a named salt
Use the warm, add-to-excess, filter, concentrate and crystallise method
Explain why excess solid and filtration are needed
Evaluate choices that affect purity and yield

blocks.learningGoal: Carry out the preparation safely and in the correct sequence.

sequence: add copper(II) oxide in small portions while stirring
continue until some black solid remains
heat the blue filtrate gently to concentrate it
cool to crystallise, then filter, rinse and dry
content.safety: Wear eye protection; use a hot-water bath or electric heater; do not boil or heat to dryness.

blocks.learningGoal: Recognise a safe, scientifically plausible crystallisation setup.

content.representation: realistic evaporating basin containing blue copper sulfate solution in a hot-water bath on an electric hot plate
content.accessibleEquivalent: The caption and adjacent method state the apparatus, heating control and purpose in assessed text.

blocks.learningGoal: Connect the practical method to the neutralisation reaction and salt naming.
Explain how each separation step improves purity and recovery.

decisions: excess insoluble solid ensures all acid is neutralised
gentle evaporation concentrates rather than dries the solution
a little cold distilled water removes solution with minimal crystal loss

blocks.learningGoal: Choose an appropriate salt-preparation route from reactant solubility.

content.insolubleRoute: Use excess solid and filtration for an insoluble base or carbonate.
content.solubleRoute: Use titration when both reactants are soluble because excess cannot be filtered off.

blocks.learningGoal: Demonstrate secure method, chemistry and evaluation reasoning.

diagnostic.stem: Identify the acid used to make a sulfate.
Identify the best endpoint for evaporation.

guided.stem: Explain why copper(II) oxide is added to excess.
Choose a method for a salt from two soluble reactants.

independent.stem: Name the salt formed from nitric acid and magnesium oxide.
Explain why some copper(II) oxide should remain.
Identify what passes through the filter paper.
Explain why the solution is not heated to dryness.
Predict the effect of washing crystals with much warm water.

exit.stem: State when titration is used instead.
